lessons.title: Introduction to Kotlin Multiplatform
lessons.content: KMP shares Kotlin code across Android, iOS, desktop, and web while keeping native UI per platform. Real scenario: sharing your LessonRepository and sync logic with a future iOS app.

lessons.title: The Shared Module Structure
lessons.content: commonMain holds platform-agnostic code; androidMain/iosMain provide actual implementations. Real scenario: domain models and repository logic in commonMain, Room swapped for SQLDelight if going multiplatform.

codeSnippets.code:
// shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/ - shared business logic
// shared/src/androidMain/kotlin/ - Android-specific implementations

lessons.title: expect / actual Mechanism
lessons.content: expect declares an API in common code; each platform provides an actual matching implementation. Real scenario: a DateFormatter needing java.text on Android but Foundation on iOS.

lessons.title: Sharing Business Logic
lessons.content: Validation rules, calculations, and domain models are prime candidates for sharing. Real scenario: sharing your content-sync version-diffing logic between Android and iOS.

lessons.title: Sharing the Network Layer
lessons.content: Ktor's client works natively on Android and iOS, making it standard for a shared network layer. Real scenario: your GitHubContentApi class could move to commonMain almost unchanged.

lessons.title: Sharing the Database Layer
lessons.content: Room is Android-only, so KMP projects typically use SQLDelight for a shared local database. Real scenario: migrating from Room to SQLDelight to share the data layer with iOS.

lessons.title: Compose Multiplatform (UI Sharing)
lessons.content: Extends Jetpack Compose beyond Android to iOS, desktop, and web, sharing UI code too. Real scenario: an internal admin tool sharing UI across desktop and Android, versus native per-platform UI for consumer apps.
